title: Tokens and themes
description: What to do when NYSDS has no component for what you need: build it from tokens so it follows every theme and release.

presets.title: Check in this order
presets.description: Reach for a component first, then a utility class, and write token CSS only for what is left.
presets.notes: Ask the room what they do first when they need a new piece of UI. Then walk the three steps. Most UI that feels custom turns out to be a component plus a few utility classes. Token CSS comes last, and it covers only what the first two can't. This list is itself nys-processlist, so the slide follows its own advice.
presets.html: Docs: Components · Utilities · Tokens

presets.title: When the search comes back empty
presets.description: NYSDS has no component for an application summary, so you check the near misses before you build one.
presets.notes: The running example for this deck is an application summary: label and value pairs, a status, and a Change link on each row. A search of the component docs, or the NYSDS MCP's find_components, for "summary", "description list", and "key value" finds no direct match. Go through the near misses out loud. nys-table is for comparing rows of data, and this is one record. Someone will ask why the summary isn't a nys-card. The card exposes custom properties for height and type only, so you can't theme its border or background, and you can't add the title band and accent. nys-badge fits one row exactly, so it goes inside what you build. Build only the part nothing covers.
presets.html:
You need an application summary: label and value pairs, a status, and a Change link on each row. A search for "summary", "description list", and "key value" finds no match.

The closest components, and whether they fit
ComponentWhat it's forFit
nys-tableComparing many records across columnsNo. You have one record.
nys-cardGrouping content about one subjectNo. Its border and background aren't themeable.
nys-badgeShowing a statusYes. Use it inside what you build.

presets.title: Primitives and applied tokens
presets.description: A primitive names a value and an applied token names a job, so you build with the applied ones.
presets.notes: Start with the name. Every token starts with --nys, then a category (color, font, space, radius, border), then the job, then a variant. Color variants are emphasis words: faint, weaker, weak, mid, strong, stronger. Scales use numbers or sizes: space-200, radius-lg. Color has two tiers. A primitive, such as --nys-color-state-blue-700, is a raw value. An applied token, such as --nys-color-theme, names a job and points at a primitive. find_tokens hides color primitives unless you ask for them, and every applied token carries a USE FOR description, which is where the middle column comes from. Point out that link and focus share one primitive today. They name different jobs, so a release can split them without breaking you. Live: add class="nys-theme-health" to the tiers div. Both theme swatches on the left turn purple. Every primitive stays put, and so do text, link, and focus. That is the theme section in one move.
presets.html:
Read a name left to right: --nys-color-text-weak is the system, the category, the job, and a variant.

Each applied token points to a primitive
Applied token: use thisUse it forPrimitive behind it
--nys-color-themePrimary buttons and key accents--nys-color-state-blue-700
--nys-color-theme-weakBorders and light accents--nys-color-state-blue-100
--nys-color-textBody copy and headings--nys-color-neutral-900
--nys-color-linkInline links--nys-color-blue-600
--nys-color-focusFocus outlines--nys-color-blue-600

presets.title: One tier for space, radius, and borders
presets.description: Spacing, radius, and border width have no applied tier, so you pick a step on the scale instead of a pixel value.
presets.notes: get_token_graph shows aliases only for color, type, and icon size. Space, radius, and border width are a single scale. You don't pick 18px. You pick --nys-space-200 or --nys-space-250, and the next release can retune the whole scale at once. The spacing utilities use the same steps, so nys-padding-300 and var(--nys-space-300) are the same size in every release. The utilities emit literal pixel values, though, so overriding a token in :root changes only the var() side. Every sample here is drawn from the token it names.
presets.html:

Type has two tiers, like color. Use a role token such as --nys-font-size-ui-md, or a nys-font-* class.

presets.title: Start with semantic markup
presets.description: A description list tells everyone, including screen readers, that these are label and value pairs.
presets.notes: No classes and no CSS yet. The NYSDS reset and type styles already make it readable. dl, dt, and dd say these are pairs, which a stack of divs can't. nys-badge is the one component that fits, so it goes inside. Each Change link has an aria-label that starts with its visible text, so a screen reader hears "Change applicant" instead of three identical links.

presets.title: Lay it out with utility classes
presets.description: Grid, spacing, and type utilities handle the layout, so the summary still has no CSS of its own.
presets.notes: Every class here comes from get_utility_classes. Each row is a 12-column grid row: the label takes 4 columns at tablet and up, the value fills the rest, and the Change link sizes to its content. On a phone, each part stacks. The type classes set family, size, and line height together. Resize the preview to show the stack. The default h2, dl, and dd margins still show, and the next step clears them.

presets.title: Style the rest with tokens
presets.description: One hook class and a few token rules add the border, radius, title band, weight, and dividers.
presets.notes: Now there is CSS, and every value in it is a token: applied tokens for color, and scale steps for radius and border width, which have no applied tier. The top accent, the title band, and the dividers use the theme family, so they will follow an agency theme. Label weight is here because NYSDS has no font-weight utility. Live: change --nys-radius-lg to --nys-radius-xl, or --nys-border-width-lg to --nys-border-width-md, and watch the steps move on the scale.

presets.title: Add the states the stylesheet can't
presets.description: The stylesheet already styles links, so you add the state it can't know about: which row the keyboard is in.
presets.notes: Go back to the last slide first and tab through: the Change links already have a focus ring and a hover underline, from the NYSDS stylesheet. What the stylesheet can't know is that your rows exist. Live: type the one rule, then press Tab into the preview. The row the keyboard is in gets a --nys-color-theme-weaker tint and a bar in --nys-color-focus, the same focus color nys-* components use. Link text stays above 5.8 to 1 contrast on the tint in all eight themes.

presets.title: How themes work
presets.description: A nys-theme class remaps the --nys-color-theme family for everything inside it and leaves every other token alone.
presets.notes: Eight tiles, one set of CSS rules. Each tile draws four steps of the theme family, from --nys-color-theme-weak to --nys-color-theme-stronger, and its class picks the palette. Put the class on html or body for a whole site, or on any element to theme one section. A theme nested inside another theme wins. Default is the absence of a class: in 1.23.1, nys-theme-default does not reset a parent theme. A data-theme attribute, which the docs site shows, works the same as the class. The MCP themes guide recommends data-nys-theme, but no 1.23.1 stylesheet selects on it, so don't use it. Themes change only the theme family. Text, links, focus, and status colors such as success and danger stay the same in every theme, so contrast and meaning hold.
presets.html:
• Default (NY.gov)

  • Administration
    nys-theme-admin

presets.title: Switch the theme
presets.description: The token-built summary changes with the nys-* components, and the hard-coded copy stays NY.gov blue.
presets.notes: Pick each theme in turn. The buttons, toggle, checkbox, and the summary built on tokens all change together. The hard-coded copy on the right matches in the default theme until you hover or tab, and it never changes theme. Nobody can tell the two apart until a theme or a release ships, and then the hard-coded one is wrong everywhere it was copied. The badge and the Change links stay the same in every theme on purpose: status and link colors are not theme tokens. The script swaps one nys-theme-* class on the wrapper. Default removes the class.

presets.title: Build with tokens: a checklist
presets.description: Run through this list the next time a component search comes back empty.
presets.notes: This is the deck in seven lines. If someone remembers one thing, make it the fourth line: an applied token when one exists, a scale step otherwise, never a hex value. The last line matters as much: every gap you log is evidence the design system team uses to decide what to build next.
presets.html:
Search the component docs, or the NYSDS MCP's find_components, with two or three synonyms, and check the near misses Start with semantic HTML, and put nys-* components inside it Lay it out with utility classes Style the rest with tokens: an applied token when one exists, a scale step otherwise, never a hex value Add the states the stylesheet can't, such as which row has focus Switch themes and confirm it follows Log the gap and tell the design system team

Docs: Tokens · Themes

presets.title: Ask for a component
presets.description: Propose a new component when more than one team needs it or when its behavior is hard to get right.
presets.notes: Building with tokens is the right move for one app. It is the wrong move for the fifth app to build the same thing. The questions in the right column come from the proposal process on the Contribute page. Your token-built version is a strong example to bring, because the design system team can see exactly which tokens it needed. State employees can also ask in the NYSDS Teams channel or at office hours, which the Contribute page links.
presets.html:
Ask the design system team when

A second team needs the same thing It has keyboard, focus, or ARIA behavior that is hard to get right No applied color token fits the job, so you reached for a color primitive or a hex value

Bring

Why it belongs in the design system How you expect it to work Examples, including the version you built with tokens

Search the existing proposals in NYSDS GitHub Discussions first. If nothing matches, open a new one.
